claim: Evidence bullet: "Across multi-stage service settings including restaurants, the wait before service (the entry/host-stand wait) had the largest influence on overall service evaluation of the stages studied." (2015, inderscience.com artid=67435)
problem: Scope is misstated. The abstract says the service-entry wait had the largest influence in restaurant services only; in the assessment services the service-exit wait was predominant and in the dental services the in-service wait was most important. Presented as a finding across settings, it is contradicted by the source. The same over-general wording is echoed in problem.summary point (2).
fix: Rewrite to: "In a multi-stage field study across restaurants, assessment and dental services, the service-entry wait had the largest influence on service evaluation in the restaurant setting (elsewhere the exit or in-service wait dominated)." Keep the restaurant-only scope in problem.summary too.

claim: measured_outcomes entry 2 (De Vries, Roy & De Koster 2018, Journal of Operations Management) strength = "High"
problem: Single-site study (one Indian restaurant in Bangalore, 94,404 customer groups, Feb 2016-Jan 2017). The brief's own finding text says "Single-restaurant setting, so treat effect sizes as site-specific", and the brief rates another single-restaurant study (the 2025 YOLOv8 paper) only Medium. High is inconsistent with both.
fix: Downgrade to Medium and note it is a single-restaurant field study plus simulation, not a multi-site replication.

claim: legal_privacy: "GC 23-02 is no longer in force" marked confirmed: true, citing only https://www.nlrb.gov/guidance/memos-research/general-counsel-memos
problem: The cited NLRB memos index establishes GC 25-05 ("Rescission of Certain General Counsel Memoranda", 02/14/2025) and shows rescission tags on several Abruzzo-era memos, but the page slice I could read does not itself show GC 23-02 being rescinded. The specific rescission of GC 23-02 rests on the law-firm summary the brief mentions, and the GC 25-05 document still returns an unsupported content type (application/octet-stream) when fetched, as the brief itself notes in data_gaps. Marking it confirmed while the supporting text could not be read overstates the evidence.
fix: Set confirmed: false (or cite the law-firm summary explicitly as the source for the rescission of GC 23-02) and keep the existing caveat text.

claim: legal_privacy GC 23-02 entry quotes the memo as covering "intrusive or abusive electronic monitoring and automated management practices"
problem: Not a verbatim quote. The memo's language is "intrusive or abusive methods of electronic surveillance and automated management"; the subject line is "Electronic Monitoring and Algorithmic Management of Employees Interfering with the Exercise of Section 7 Rights".
fix: Quote the actual phrase, or drop the quotation marks and paraphrase.

claim: measured_outcomes entry 3 (2025 JAIDA YOLOv8 table detector) sample = "One restaurant, custom dataset, 90/10 train-test split"
problem: The 90/10 split in that paper applies to the 1,344-record occupancy time-series dataset used for the Exponential Smoothing / Random Forest forecasting models. The detector's metrics (mAP@0.5 0.997, mAP@0.5:0.95 0.985) are reported on a "Custom Validation Set", and no train/test split ratio is given for the detection dataset. The numbers themselves are correct.
fix: Describe the sample as "one restaurant, custom-annotated table images, metrics on a validation set" and leave the 90/10 split to the forecasting component.

claim: buyers[0] size_where_it_matters: "below ~10 tables the walk-around is cheaper than the system"
problem: The cited practitioner write-up says the dining room must be small at "5-8 tables" for walking the floor to be cheaper; it does not support a ~10-table cut-off. The 15+ tables threshold elsewhere in the brief is stated correctly.
fix: Change to "below roughly 5-8 tables the walk-around is cheaper" or drop the number.

claim: pilot.cost_range: "$2,500-$5,500 one-time (cameras ~$800-1,500, edge box $250-450, network/cabling $300-800, 2-4 days install and calibration at $75-125/hr)"
problem: The components do not reconcile with the stated band: the upper bound sums to about $6,750 (1,500 + 450 + 800 + 4 days x 8 h x $125), not $5,500; the camera range also starts at $800 while 4 cameras x $150 = $600.
fix: Widen the envelope (e.g. $2,500-$6,500) or restate the install-hour assumption, and set the camera line to $600-1,500.

claim: data_gaps: "LFM2.5-VL release dates were not shown on the blog pages I read"
problem: The LFM2.5-VL-3B post carries a citation line dated "Aug 2026" and the model page links fine-tuning docs, so the absence claim is inaccurate (harmless, but it is a stated gap that is not a gap).
fix: Either cite "Aug 2026" from the blog's citation line or drop the item from data_gaps.
